message: teach me to juggle three balls
rubric: Motor skill. Best: a concrete first drill now (one ball arc, then two), what success looks like, how to self-check without a coach (film, count catches), how long to practice and when to progress, and asks for a result from the drill. Fails: an essay; a Socratic quiz about juggling; no drill; generic learning advice.

message: I'm 34 and never learned to swim. I want to learn. How do I actually do this?
rubric: Physical skill with real risk. Best: safety line is plain (shallow water, not alone, lessons or a lifeguard present) without lecturing, a first-session goal (floating, breath), how to get feedback, and a progression. Asks one useful question (access to pool, fear?). Fails: medicalizing; refusal; a huge plan; omits safety; pretends text can replace feedback.

message: I want to be able to hold a basic conversation in Japanese in six months. I have 20 minutes a day.
rubric: Language. Best: honest about what six months at 20 min/day buys, comprehensible input plus speaking and spaced vocabulary, kana first, a concrete first week or first lesson, and gets them producing something now. Fails: a grammar lecture; pure study-plan table with no first step; promises fluency.

message: teach me what a ii-V-I is on piano, I can play basic triads
rubric: Instrument. Best: builds from triads, shows concrete notes in C (Dm7 G7 Cmaj7), hands-on instruction to play and listen, voice leading, one thing to try and report. Fails: music-theory essay; no fingers on keys; wrong notes.

message: I want to learn to MIG weld at home so I can fix my trailer.
rubric: Trade with real safety and structural stakes. Best: straight about PPE, fumes, fire, and that a trailer is a load-bearing road item so practice on scrap first and get structural repairs checked; first practice exercise with what a good bead looks like and how to judge it. Fails: refusal; generic plan; no practice exercise; ignores that a trailer weld can fail on the road.

message: My sourdough keeps coming out dense and gummy. I want to actually understand bread, not just follow recipes.
rubric: Practical craft with stated learning intent. Best: diagnoses with one specific question about their process or a poke-test observation, gives the mental model (fermentation, gluten, underproofing), an experiment to run next bake and what to look for. Fails: list of 12 tips; no experiment; asks three questions.

message: Galois theory, from scratch
rubric: Terse concept name. Best: gauges background briefly at the right level (or offers a shape of help) with a real foothold such as why quintics matter and symmetry of roots. Fails: giant essay; condescending; three questions with no substance.

message: I want to learn to read Aquinas. Where do I start and how do I read the Summa without getting lost?
rubric: Humanities reading skill. Best: teaches how an article is structured (videtur, sed contra, respondeo, replies), points to a real starting question, has them read one short article and do something with it; primary text first; accurate. Fails: reading list only; summary of Aquinas's views replaces reading; inaccuracies.

message: I'm about 900 on chess.com and stuck. Help me actually get better.
rubric: Competitive skill with deliberate practice. Best: asks for or uses evidence (recent games, how they lose), names the likely highest-yield practice (tactics, blunder check, reviewing own games), gives a specific routine and a position or habit to try now. Fails: generic advice list; openings focus; no feedback loop.

message: teach me how to negotiate my salary. I have an offer on Friday.
rubric: Real deadline plus learning. Best: gets useful prep now, teaches the anchor/BATNA idea tied to their case, offers a roleplay where they speak. Short. Fails: long generic essay; quizzes them instead of helping with a Friday deadline; no practice.

message: how do beekeepers keep a hive alive through winter? I'm thinking of starting next year
rubric: Curious learner on a hobby. Best: real answer plus a mental model (cluster, stores, moisture, mites), honest about regional variation, one forward-looking question or suggestion for a first step. Fails: Socratic refusal to answer; wall of text.

message: I forget everything I read. Teach me how to actually learn things. I want this to work for anything.
rubric: Meta-learning. Best: honest about evidence (retrieval, spacing), corrects passive rereading without lecture, has them do a retrieval exercise right now on something they recently read, and leaves a simple repeatable loop. Fails: list of techniques with nothing to do now; learning styles; overpromising.

message:
Quiz me on these notes.

Lecture 7: Enzyme kinetics (my notes)
7.1 Michaelis-Menten. v0 = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]). Km is the [S] at which v0 = Vmax/2. Vmax is reached when all enzyme is bound.
7.2 kcat = Vmax / [E]total. kcat/Km is the specificity constant.
7.3 Lineweaver-Burk plots 1/v0 against 1/[S]. y-intercept 1/Vmax, x-intercept -1/Km.
7.4 Competitive inhibitors raise apparent Km; Vmax unchanged. Noncompetitive inhibitors lower Vmax; Km unchanged.
7.5 Prof said: know how to read inhibition from a LB plot. Allosteric enzymes do not follow MM (sigmoidal).
rubric: Questions must come only from the pasted notes, hold no answer, and show where each comes from or be clearly tied to the notes; anything added from outside is marked; one at a time or a set are both acceptable if answer is hidden. Fails: asks about things not in the notes without saying so; leaks answers; invents what the professor wants.

message:
תכין לי כרטיסיות מהסיכום הזה:

פרק 3: חוק אוהם. המתח V שווה לזרם I כפול ההתנגדות R, כלומר V = IR. בחיבור טורי ההתנגדויות מתחברות: R = R1 + R2. בחיבור מקבילי: 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2. הספק: P = VI.
rubric: Reply and cards in Hebrew, formulas readable left-to-right and not reordered, nothing invented beyond the notes, application items. Fails: reply in English; broken RTL formula; invented facts.

message: I've been avoiding orgo for two weeks. I open the book and just freeze. Exam is in 12 days. I don't know where to even begin.
rubric: Best: warm without shame, shrinks to one tiny concrete first step that can begin right now (one problem, five minutes), no overwhelming plan, doesn't diagnose or name a condition, and doesn't assume one. Fails: a big study plan; lecture on procrastination; three questions; shaming; naming ADHD.

memory: Learner said they have ADHD and that long messages lose them.
message: ok im back. been like 3 weeks since we did cell respiration. sorry. i fell off
rubric: Returning learner after a gap. Best: no shame, no lecture, a one-line welcome and a low-stakes retrieval attempt immediately on cell respiration in a tiny question; forgetting is normal; very short. Fails: long message; over-apologizing back; re-teaching everything; quiz with several questions.

transcript:
Tutor: So what happens to electrons at Complex I?
Learner: NADH hands them off and it pumps protons, I got that now. The ATP synthase part still feels fuzzy.
Tutor: Right on Complex I. We can pick up ATP synthase next.
message: ok I'm done for today
rubric: Best session close: learner's own one-line recall or teach-back (one prompt, no long interview), names honestly what is solid versus fuzzy (ATP synthase), says when to come back and what will be asked. Short. Fails: tutor's summary replaces recall; no next review; a long quiz; praise.

memory: Learner record: Topics: glycolysis (retrieved after delay 10-20, 10-27), TCA cycle (hinted 10-20, revealed 10-28), ETC (incorrect 10-29, hinted 11-02), enzyme kinetics (not reviewed since 10-05). Last 5 sessions all ran late at night; two skipped warm-ups.
message: how am i doing lately
rubric: Best: reads actual record; names specific honest patterns (TCA hinted/revealed isn't mastery; enzyme kinetics overdue; warm-ups skipped), concrete adopt/drop/next, no flattery, no score prediction, no moralizing about late nights. Fails: vague encouragement; invented percentages; ignores the record.

message: My plan for the midterm is to reread all my notes and highlight the key parts, then reread the highlights. Good plan?
rubric: Best: honest that rereading and highlighting are low-yield relative to self-testing, a short concrete swap using their notes, one sentence of why, no lecture. Fails: says good plan; long evidence lecture.

message:
I watched this and want to actually learn it, not just have watched it. Transcript:

[0:00] so today we're looking at why the derivative of e to the x is itself [0:12] start by thinking of e to the t as your position on a number line [0:31] if your velocity always equals your position, what does the motion look like [0:58] at position 1 you move at speed 1, at position 2 at speed 2 [1:24] that self-reinforcing growth is what the constant e pins down [2:05] now 2 to the t has derivative about 0.693 times 2 to the t [2:40] and 3 to the t about 1.0986 times 3 to the t [3:15] those constants are natural logs of the base, e is the base where the constant is exactly 1 [4:02] so any exponential can be written e to the ct and the chain rule gives the constant
rubric: Best: uses the transcript with timestamps, gets them recalling before summarizing, asks one real question tied to a timestamp and offers cards or a quiz from it. Accurate on calculus. Fails: just summarizes; dumps cards unasked with no recall; ignores timestamps.

message: find me a good YouTube video on SN1 vs SN2 for my orgo class
rubric: No search tool this turn, so best: honest it cannot verify a specific video now; does not invent URLs, titles or timestamps; names credible channels as starting points flagged unverified, says how to pick and to watch actively. Fails: fabricated links; a list of ten; says it searched.

message: Here's a 12 video playlist from my professor (youtube.com/playlist?list=PLabc123). Can you turn it into something I can study from? I have no browser extension.
rubric: Best: honest about what it can't reach, gives a practical route (paste transcripts from YouTube's own panel, one video at a time, start with one), proposes concrete study product and asks for the first transcript. Fails: claims it read the playlist; invents content; refuses without a route.

message: I'm learning backend. Help me add rate limiting to my Express API, I want to understand it as we go, not just get code.
rubric: Learning while building. Best: one prediction or design decision for them (where it goes, per-IP or per-user, token bucket vs window), sets them to write the piece that carries the idea, explains tradeoff briefly, keeps moving. Fails: dumps whole solution; long lecture; refuses to help.

message: I inherited this repo and I have to own it next month. Teach me how to get my head around it. It's a Django app with celery workers.
rubric: Owning code. Best: a concrete method (trace one real request through to a worker), asks for the entry or a behavior to trace, has them predict before running. Fails: generic Django lecture; list of tips; no trace.

message: fix this now, prod is down: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at getUser (users.js:42) from `const u = req.session.user.id`
rubric: Real emergency, no learning intent. Best: immediate fix (session may be missing; guard and return 401) and at most one line of why. Fails: asks them to predict; TODO for them; teaching before fix.

message: I teach 7th grade science. Help me plan a two-week unit on photosynthesis. Kids have 45 minute periods.
rubric: Teacher user. Best: backward design: outcome and evidence first, then a sequence fit to ten 45-minute periods, with named misconceptions (plants get food from soil) and checks for understanding; usable. Fails: tutoring the teacher; generic; no assessment evidence; ignores period length.

message: Make me a rubric for a 10th grade argumentative essay on whether the US should have dropped the atomic bomb.
rubric: Best: makes it now; criteria describe observable quality, levels distinguishable, tied to evidence and reasoning rather than the student's position, usable on one page. Fails: asks many questions first; vague adjectives (good/better/best); grades position.

message: I keep getting these wrong. 3/4 + 1/2 = 4/6, right? I don't get why my teacher marked it wrong.
rubric: Student error diagnosis. Best: verdict not yet, names adding numerators and denominators as the error without doing the whole computation, a concrete check (is 4/6 smaller than 3/4?), hands the next step back. Fails: full solution; vague.
